evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Etymology Database, CUHK)
evidence.text: The entry reports oracle-bone 一 used as a numeral and gives the example 《合集》21575「一牛」 (‘one ox’). This supports an early numeric use, but the accessible result does not provide a date for that inscription.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — Oracle-bone entry for 一

evidence.source: 說文解字在線查詢 Shuowen.org
evidence.field: 一 entry; seal form and historical explanation
evidence.text: The entry prints the received Shuowen definition 惟初太始，道立於一，造分天地，化成萬物 and says forms in the 一 category derive from 一. It also labels 弌 as 古文一. This is a Han lexicographic and cosmological account, not independent proof of the graph’s earliest origin. The page includes Duan Yucai’s later note classifying 一 as an indicative graph, which is an interpretive classification rather than paleographic evidence.
evidence.title: 說文解字「一」

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, supplementary materials for Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction
evidence.text: The table lists 一 with Mandarin yī, Middle Chinese 'jit (with its analysis), Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *ʔi[t], gloss ‘one’, and GSR 0394a. The local row in sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv agrees exactly: MC 'jit and OC *ʔi[t]. The modern Mandarin and reconstructed historical forms are readings of the character/word, not evidence for a graphic component or borrowing.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, sorted by radical and stroke number

evidence.field: Unihan U+4E00; kMandarin and reading fields
evidence.text: Official Unihan record for U+4E00 gives kMandarin yī. It also records readings including Cantonese jat1, Korean IL, Japanese on readings ICHI/ITSU, and Vietnamese nhất. The repository’s local Unihan_Readings.txt row for 一 is kMandarin yī, matching the official record. These are current metadata and do not establish the ancient graphic history.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+4E00

evidence.field: database scope and stated paleographic resources
evidence.text: The database guide says the resource covers oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, small-seal, and regular-script forms, and links shape, sound, meaning, and dictionary indexes. This establishes the database’s relevant scope, but the character-specific 一 evolution record could not be opened during this research, so no sequence of individual glyph shapes is asserted here.

evidence.text: The dossier’s suggestions that 一 represents heaven, earth, or the number one are not equally supported by the sources inspected. The CUHK entry supports numeral use in oracle-bone writing; Shuowen supplies a cosmological interpretation but does not establish that the graph originally depicted heaven or earth. No inspected paleographic source supports the heaven/earth graphic-origin alternatives.

A character-specific, visually inspected sequence of oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, seal, clerical, and regular forms was not obtained. Exact graphic transitions, alleged corruption, and any detailed chronological claims remain unverified.

No independent evidence was found in this bounded search to establish semantic extensions such as ‘alone’ chronologically; current dictionary definitions should not be read as an ordered semantic history.

No phonetic or semantic components apply to the character’s basic graph analysis as researched here; it is treated in the inspected sources as a numeral graph. No sound-component comparison or loan analysis is warranted by the cited findings.
The dossier’s Proto-Sino-Tibetan reconstruction and Min dialect forms were outside the primary evidence recovered in this pass; this report does not validate or refute them.
